# Differential expression and GSEA

This chapter covers the analysis half of TTpipe (`run_analysis: true`): what
DESeq2, fgsea and the Sankey step do, which files they write, and how to
read them. The code (`scripts/run_deseq2.R`, `make_rnk.R`, `run_fgsea.R`,
`make_sankey.R`) was written without being run locally, and only its plain-R
helper functions are unit-tested, so check the first real results with some
care ([Validation status](validation.qmd)).

## What goes in

| Input | Source |
|-------|--------|
| Count matrix | `counts/counts_deseq2.txt` from the pipeline, or the file named in `analysis_counts` (genes x samples, first column `gene_id`, header = sample `Name`s, integer counts) |
| Sample table | `counts/samples_deseq2.txt` (`sample`, `condition`, `replicate`), written from the samplesheet |
| Gene table | `counts/gene_info.tsv`, built from your GTF (needed to turn gene ids into symbols for GSEA) |

DESeq2 matches the matrix columns to the sample table **by name**. If the
names differ in any way, it stops and lists which names are only in the table
and which only in the matrix, rather than silently reordering.

## DESeq2

One job (`deseq2`) handles every comparison. In order:

1. **Prefilter.** Keep a gene only if it has at least `min_count` counts (default
   10) in at least `min_samples` samples (default 2). The log prints how many
   genes pass. Everything below (normalised counts, VST, results, the Sankey,
   the ranked lists) contains only these genes.
2. **VST and PCA.** A variance-stabilising transformation (`blind = FALSE`, so
   it uses the design) and a PCA of the samples coloured by condition and
   shaped by replicate (`analysis/figures/pca.pdf`). With fewer than 1000
   genes passing the prefilter, which only happens with tiny test data,
   TTpipe uses `varianceStabilizingTransformation()` instead of `vst()`
   because `vst()` needs at least 1000 genes.
3. **The DESeq2 model.** Size factors, dispersions and a Wald test, with the
   `design` from the config (default `~ condition + replicate`). The design may
   use only the columns `condition` and `replicate`, and must include
   `condition`; anything else is an error.
4. **Results per comparison.** For each `[treatment, reference]` pair,
   `results(contrast = c("condition", treatment, reference), alpha = alpha,
   lfcThreshold = lfc_threshold)`. The reference level is `reference_condition`;
   the default comparisons are every other condition against it.

### What `~ condition + replicate` assumes

`replicate` is a batch term: samples with the same replicate label (for
example every `rep1`) are treated as sharing a batch effect. That is right if
replicate 1 of each condition was grown and processed together, as in a
time course done in parallel. If your replicates are independent, with no
shared batch across conditions, use `design: '~ condition'` instead
([Recipes](recipes.qmd#custom-comparisons-and-design)). The guide uses
`~ time + replicate`; TTpipe's `condition` is that same variable under a
different name.

### Output files

All under `analysis/deseq2/` unless noted.

| File | Contents |
|------|----------|
| `degs_<treatment>_vs_<reference>.csv` | The full results table: one row per gene that passed the prefilter. Columns: `gene_id`, `baseMean`, `log2FoldChange`, `lfcSE`, `stat`, `pvalue`, `padj`. Comma-separated |
| `deg_summary.tsv` | `comparison`, `n_up`, `n_down`, `n_tested` per comparison |
| `normalized_counts.tsv` | Counts divided by the DESeq2 size factors (genes passing the prefilter; tab-separated, first column `gene_id`) |
| `vst.tsv` | The VST values (same layout), used for the PCA in the QC report |
| `sankey_categories.tsv` | Up / Down / n.s. category per gene and comparison |
| `../figures/pca.pdf` | PCA of the samples |

### How to read a results table

- **`log2FoldChange`**: positive means more new RNA in the *treatment* than in the
  *reference* (for `6H_vs_DMSO`, higher at 6 h than in DMSO). A value of 1 is a
  doubling.
- **`baseMean`**: average normalised count over all samples; a measure of
  how much signal the gene has.
- **`lfcSE`**: standard error of the log2 fold change.
- **`stat`**: the Wald statistic, `log2FoldChange / lfcSE` when
  `lfc_threshold` is 0. It is what GSEA ranks by.
- **`pvalue`, `padj`**: the raw and the Benjamini-Hochberg adjusted p-values.
  Use `padj`. TTpipe's default cut-off is **0.01** with **no fold-change
  threshold** (the guide's choice for TT-seq).
- **`NA` in `padj`**: standard DESeq2 behaviour: its automatic independent
  filtering gives low-count genes an `NA` adjusted p-value, and a gene with an
  extreme outlier count can get `NA` too. `n_tested` in `deg_summary.tsv` is
  the number of genes with a non-`NA` `padj`.

`n_up` and `n_down` count genes with `padj < alpha` and a positive or negative
`log2FoldChange`.

::: {.callout-warning}
**`lfc_threshold` above 0 changes the meaning of `stat`.** DESeq2 then tests
whether |log2 fold change| exceeds the threshold, and `stat` is the statistic of
that test, not `log2FoldChange / lfcSE`. Ranking by it for GSEA is then no
longer the guide's ranking. The default, 0, matches the guide.
:::

### No spike-in

DESeq2's normalisation assumes most genes do not change. There is no spike-in
in this pipeline, so a treatment that changes nascent transcription globally
cannot be detected from these results, and "down" always means "down relative
to the bulk of genes". See [From Reads to Results](journey.qmd#what-the-numbers-do-not-tell-you).

## GSEA with fgsea

GSEA (gene-set enrichment analysis) asks whether the genes of a set, such as a
pathway, cluster toward the top or the bottom of a ranked list of all genes.
TTpipe runs it with the R package **fgsea**, once for each combination of gene-set
collection and comparison, and only when `gsea_collections` lists `.gmt`
files.

1. **Ranked list** (`analysis/gsea/<comparison>.rnk`, rule `rnk`). Genes ranked
   by the DESeq2 Wald statistic, written as `symbol<TAB>stat`, sorted from
   highest to lowest. The symbol is the `gene_name` from your GTF. Genes with no
   statistic or no symbol are dropped, and if two genes share a symbol the one
   with the larger |stat| is kept. If every gene is dropped, the rule stops with
   an error: this happens when the count matrix's gene ids do not match the GTF's
   (for example an analysis-only matrix made with another annotation).
2. **fgsea** (`analysis/gsea/<collection>_<comparison>.tsv`, rule `fgsea`).
   Weighted scoring (`gseaParam = 1`, the guide's "weighted"), gene-set size limits
   `gsea_min_size` / `gsea_max_size` (defaults 1 and 1000000: no filter, as in the
   guide) and a fixed seed `gsea_seed` (default 42). p-values come from fgsea's
   adaptive multilevel procedure, not from 10000 permutations.

| Column | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `pathway` | Gene-set name from the `.gmt` file |
| `size` | Genes of the set found in the ranked list |
| `ES` | Enrichment score |
| `NES` | Normalised enrichment score (comparable across sets) |
| `pval`, `padj` | p-value and its Benjamini-Hochberg adjustment over the sets tested |
| `leadingEdge` | The genes driving the enrichment, separated by `;` |

Rows are sorted by `pval`. **Positive `NES`**: the set sits toward the top of the
list, that is toward genes more transcribed in the treatment than the reference.
**Negative `NES`**: toward genes less transcribed. Look at `padj` (the run log
prints how many sets have `padj < 0.05`); a set is more convincing when its
leading-edge genes are ones you also see in the DEG table.

::: {.callout-note}
fgsea replaces the Java GSEA 4.3.2 desktop tool the guide uses, and ranks by
gene symbol where the guide ranks by `gene_id`. The results should be similar
in kind, not identical. TTpipe's authors have not compared the two.
:::

**Gene-set symbols must match your GTF's `gene_name`.** MSigDB mouse collections
use mouse symbols; a human collection against a mouse GTF will find few genes.
Set sizes in the table show how many genes of each set were found.

## The Sankey diagram

`analysis/figures/sankey.pdf` follows the genes that were tested in **every**
comparison. For each comparison, each gene is classified:

- **Up**: `padj < alpha` and `log2FoldChange > 0`;
- **Down**: `padj < alpha` and `log2FoldChange < 0`;
- **n.s.** (not significant): everything else, including genes whose `padj` is `NA`.

The diagram has one vertical axis per comparison, labelled with the treatment
condition (`2H`, `6H`, `24H`) when all comparisons share one reference, and with
the full comparison name otherwise. Bands connect the categories from one axis to
the next, and the band colour is the gene's category on the **first** axis, so you
can see where genes that were up at 2 h end up at 6 h and 24 h. Colours are green
for Down, magenta for Up and grey for n.s. The count of genes in each category is
printed in the axis.

`analysis/deseq2/sankey_categories.tsv` is the table behind it (`gene_id` and a
category per comparison), which you can reuse for your own plots.

With only **one comparison** a flow diagram has nothing to flow between, so TTpipe
draws a bar chart of the Up, Down and n.s. counts instead. If the labelled-axes
variant of the plot cannot be built with the installed `ggforce`, the script falls
back to plain grey axes.

## The results explorer {#results-explorer}

`analysis/TTpipe_results_explorer.html` (written when `results_explorer: true`,
the default; also in analysis-only runs) lets you look at the DESeq2 and GSEA
results without writing code. It is one static file: all data are embedded as
JSON and the plotting library is inlined, so it opens by double-clicking, from
a laptop with no network, and can be emailed. Nothing is computed on a server.

**Controls.**

- *Contrast*: one entry per comparison (`<treatment>_vs_<reference>`).
- *Plot*: **Volcano** shows log2 fold change (x) against -log10(padj) (y);
  **MA** shows log10(baseMean) (x) against log2 fold change (y). Points are
  coloured Up (magenta), Down (green) or n.s. (grey), as in the Sankey.
- *padj cut-off* and *|log2FC| cut-off*: number box plus slider. They start at
  `alpha` and `lfc_threshold` from the config; changing them updates the plot,
  the Up / Down counts and the table at once. The files on disk
  (`deg_summary.tsv`, the Sankey, GSEA input) are not changed. With
  `lfc_threshold > 0` DESeq2 has already tested against that threshold, so the
  padj values and the |log2FC| filter on the page are not independent.
- *Gene biotype*: checkboxes from `gene_type` in `gene_info.tsv`
  (protein_coding and lncRNA first, other types grouped under "all other
  biotypes", with a list to pick them one by one). Unchecked types are removed
  from plot, counts and table. *Colour by biotype* colours the points by type
  instead of by Up / Down.
- *Find gene*: symbol or gene_id, prefix match, with a drop-down of matches.
  The gene is highlighted and labelled. *Label top N genes* labels the N most
  significant Up / Down genes (smallest padj).
- Hover shows gene name, gene_id, biotype, baseMean, log2FC and padj. **Click**
  a point (or a table row) to draw that gene's normalized counts per sample as
  bars, coloured by condition, from `normalized_counts.tsv`.
- *Results table*: sortable by clicking a header, filterable by call (Up and
  Down by default) and by text. 200 rows are drawn at a time (a button shows
  more). **Download CSV** saves every row matching the current filters, not only
  the rows drawn, with the contrast name in the file.
- *GSEA tab* (only when fgsea results exist): pathway, size, NES, pval, padj
  and leadingEdge for one collection and contrast, sorted by padj with NA last,
  and a text filter on pathway or gene. The leadingEdge column is cut short;
  click a cell to expand it. With no GSEA results there is no tab.

**Limits.**

- Genes with NA padj (DESeq2's independent filtering or outlier handling) are
  shown as n.s.; in the volcano they sit at y = 0. Genes with NA baseMean are
  not in the file.
- Biotype filtering uses the `gene_type` of the annotation (GENCODE). "lncRNA"
  is whatever the GTF calls lncRNA; nothing is detected de novo.
- There is no genome browser or track panel, and no eRNA calling, in this
  version. Tracks and custom feature sets are future work.
- Size: the page holds the full result tables for every contrast, so many
  contrasts and large GSEA collections make it large. The job log
  (`logs/results_explorer.log`) prints the size and warns above 40 MB.
- The page has been exercised only on synthetic data (data preparation tests
  plus its controls driven in headless Chrome). It has not yet been run on real
  pipeline output.

## Deliberate changes in the analysis

The differences from the guide that affect this chapter (the full list is in
[Configuration](configuration.qmd#deliberate-changes-from-the-source-guide)):

- the DESeq2 variable `time` is called `condition`, the `design` is validated, and
  counts are matched to samples by name;
- `vst()` falls back to `varianceStabilizingTransformation()` below 1000 genes;
- DEG tables are CSV files with a `gene_id` column (the guide: space-delimited);
- GSEA runs in fgsea with a fixed seed, adaptive multilevel p-values and ranking
  by gene symbol;
- the Sankey code was rewritten to run, and has a one-comparison fallback.

What stays as in the guide: DESeq2 `alpha` 0.01, no log2 fold-change threshold, the
prefilter of at least 10 counts in at least 2 samples, and ranking by the Wald
statistic.
